# Model output

**Generated by `scripts/model.mjs` from `assumptions.csv`. Do not edit by hand. Every number below is an assumption run through arithmetic and none of them is a finding.**

## What is in it and what is not

Income is issuance plus outside revenue, and all of it is treated as available for these bills. The bill is seats only. Engineering is not priced, so every total here is too low until the missing lines are priced. See [`engineering.md`](engineering.md).

**Left out of every total, because nobody has a number yet:**

- outside_pay (E2): No value and not in any total. We have no direct reading. Snowbridge's authors call their engineering costs far below market rates without giving the market figure
- required_staker_return (E4): Unknown. The model reports what is left for stakers and does not say if it is enough
- polkadot_inheritance (E5): Unknown and possibly the largest engineering variable. First count: of 151 commits changing code in polkadot-fellows/runtimes in the 12 months to 5 November 2026, 9 touched only Kusama paths and 88 touched Kusama and other paths. Commits are not effort
- jam_seat_hardware (E6): No reference hardware published for a production JAM node. The JAM Prime paper anchors its hardware line on a server rented today (Hetzner AX162-1, US$722.10 a month) and says production JAM requirements still need validation. Web3 Foundation scores JAM implementations on its own standard hardware, and its milestone 3 is called Kusama-level, but the prize page does not give the spec
- team_size (L3): No value and not in any total. Team size is an output of the tests in engineering.md. Stated references are 2 people to keep Polkadot connected to Ethereum and 9 on shared protocol work, neither sized for Kusama
- chains_kept (L5): Effect on cost not yet known
- who_runs_it (L6): Effect on cost not yet known
- engineer_cost (L7): Not in any total. No base. Range is two stated budgets: the engineers keeping Polkadot connected to Ethereum (Snowbridge), before a 20% company margin and called far below market by their authors, and Gossamer's all-in rate for protocol work. Fellowship active rates are US$80,000 to US$200,000 at ranks 3 to 6 and above, but some members are also paid elsewhere, so they may not be a full cost
- upside (L9): No value and not in any total. It lowers the cash bill and passes a cost to holders, so a total that leaves it out looks cheaper than it is
- collators_and_rpc (M5): Unknown for Kusama. 54 collator slots on 4 November. Polkadot's references: Ref 1832 requested about US$24,376 a month for its system-chain collators. A forum post puts Polkadot's IBP RPC bounty at almost US$300,000 for January 2026, which others there call overpriced, and we have not checked it
- migration_and_merges (M6): Unpriced
- audit (M7): Unpriced
- legal_body (M8): The Polkadot Community Foundation's request for its set-up and first year, from 2023, described as close to a bare minimum for a minimal scope. Cayman structure, Polkadot's scope. Not tested for Kusama
- metanode_hardware (M12): Our desk estimate, not tested by any operator. Polkadot's Run a Metanode spec (updated 29 October 2026, under construction) priced at Hetzner list prices on 27 November 2026. 291 is one AX102 carrying the validator, Asset Hub and People. 403 splits both collators onto one AX42. 626 adds collators for Bridge Hub, Coretime and Encointer at the Asset Hub spec, which the page does not price. Hardware and bandwidth only, every seat costed as if it collates, and the page gives no RPC or light-client load figure. Sits inside Robert Hambrock's US$300-500 and under M9's 1,200

## If one operator runs several seats: our split, not a finding

The JAM Prime paper prices every seat as its own operation. Its own table splits the US$3,000 into US$1,200 of hosting and bandwidth and US$1,800 of labour, tooling and margin. Here hardware is paid for each seat and the US$1,800 once for each operator. That split is our assumption, and some labour grows with each seat. At 2.4% issuance and 32 cores (96 seats). Kusama today runs about 1.25 seats an operator, as a floor.

| Hardware a seat | Seats an operator | Operators | Cost a seat a month | Bill a year | KSM price where the pot covers it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| US$1,200 | 1 | 96 | US$3,000 | US$3.46m | US$7.54 |
| US$1,200 | 1.25 | 77 | US$2,644 | US$3.05m | US$6.65 |
| US$1,200 | 3 | 32 | US$1,800 | US$2.07m | US$4.53 |
| US$500 | 1 | 96 | US$2,300 | US$2.65m | US$5.78 |
| US$500 | 1.25 | 77 | US$1,944 | US$2.24m | US$4.89 |
| US$500 | 3 | 32 | US$1,100 | US$1.27m | US$2.77 |
| US$300 | 1 | 96 | US$2,100 | US$2.42m | US$5.28 |
| US$300 | 1.25 | 77 | US$1,744 | US$2.01m | US$4.38 |

US$1,200 is the JAM Prime paper's hosting line. US$300 and US$500 are the ends of [Robert Hambrock's range](https://forum.polkadot.network/t/proposal-discussion-adapting-kusama-to-demand-and-its-jam-future/17141/23) for renting good validator hardware today, from his own validators. None of them is measured on a JAM node.
